h1: The 8 Best Husqvarna Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Husqvarna Leaf Blowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 Husqvarna leaf blowers compared on battery versus gas, CFM, weight and harness design, from the 230iB to the 580BTS.
summary: The Husqvarna Leaf Blaster 350iB kit is the best overall, 800 CFM on battery with the pack and charger included. The 230iB is the lightest at 8.4 lbs, and a lower-cost 350iB listing suits owners who already have a battery. The 530iB is the pro battery blower, while the 350BT, 580BTS, 360BT and 150BT cover gas backpacks.
intro: Husqvarna sells two kinds of blower that share a badge and little else. The battery handhelds start with a trigger, weigh less than ten pounds and run until the pack is empty. The gas backpacks carry their weight on your shoulders and run as long as you have fuel, which is why contractors and owners of acreage buy them. Mixing the two up is how people end up with a backpack for a patio or a battery tool that dies halfway across a lawn.

Eight blowers were ranked here: the 230iB, two 350iB listings, the 530iB and four gas models. We weighed airflow, the weight when a listing states it, power type and whether the kit ships with what you need to start. Specs that the listings omit are not guessed, and brand claims about emissions and fuel use are labeled as claims.

products.name: Husqvarna Leaf Blaster 350iB Battery Powered Cordless Leaf Blower (Kit)
products.verdict: 800 CFM on battery power, with the battery and charger in the box. The easy default.
products.description:
The 350iB kit is the Husqvarna to buy for a normal yard. It moves 800 CFM from a handheld, runs on a battery with the pack and charger included, and skips gas fumes and pull-cord starting. It sits in the $200 to $500 tier. Battery power suits frequent, short jobs: you pick it up, squeeze the trigger and put it away without mixing fuel.

It wins because it works out of the box, where the other 350iB listing may leave you shopping for a battery. It costs more than the 230iB, and the extra buys 150 CFM of airflow.

Buy it for a mid-size to large suburban lot. The caveat is runtime, which is limited by the battery, so a heavily wooded property may need a second pack. Skip it if you only sweep a patio.
products.idealFor: Suburban yards that need regular, quiet cleanup.
products.skipIf: You only clear a small patio.

products.name: Husqvarna 230iB Battery Powered Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 650 CFM at 8.4 lbs, the lightest listing here, with battery and charger included.
products.description:
The 230iB is the lightest here. It lists 650 CFM at 8.4 lbs, which the listing calls best-in-class weight, with LED power indicators and the battery and charger included, in the $200 to $500 tier. A lighter body matters because the blower hangs from one arm, and fatigue sets in long before the battery dies.

It ranks second because it moves 150 CFM less air than the 350iB. It undercuts the 350iB kit on price, and for a typical lawn that gap rarely matters.

A smart buy for people who dislike heavy tools or have shoulder trouble. The caveat: choose the 350iB if your leaves are wet or deep, because less volume means more passes. At 650 CFM it is also less suited to big piles.
cons: Costs more than other 18V class tools
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants less weight in their hands.
products.skipIf: You face thick, wet leaf piles.

products.name: Husqvarna Leaf Blaster 350iB Battery Powered Cordless Leaf Blower (Lower-Cost Listing)
products.verdict: The same 800 CFM, 200 MPH motor at the lowest price in the roundup.
products.description:
This is the second 350iB listing, with the same 800 CFM and 200 MPH motor as the kit and the lowest price in the guide. The listing says it is 15 percent lighter than comparable blowers. Air speed matters for wet leaves: 200 MPH peels matted leaves off turf where a slower stream rides over them.

It ranks below the kit because the listing is less explicit about what is in the box. If you already own a compatible Husqvarna battery and charger, it is the better buy.

Best for existing Husqvarna battery owners who want the stronger motor without paying twice for a pack. The caveat: confirm what ships before ordering, since a bare tool plus a separate battery and charger can cost much more than the kit and erase the saving.
pros: Same 800 CFM motor as the kit
products.idealFor: Owners with a Husqvarna battery system already.
products.skipIf: You need a battery and charger in the box.

products.name: Husqvarna 530iB Battery Blower
products.verdict: A pro-style battery blower with a continuous boost mode and adjustable power.
products.description:
The 530iB is Husqvarna's pro-style battery blower. It offers a continuous boost mode with no time limit, power adjustable at any level and an advanced motor and fan design aimed at working days, in the $200 to $500 tier. A boost that does not time out matters for crews, who otherwise drop to a lower setting after a short burst.

It ranks below the 350iB models because the listing gives no CFM number and the price is higher. It beats them for people who work all day and want fine control of output.

A good fit for landscapers and serious homeowners. The caveat: ask for the airflow figure before buying, since a blower with no stated CFM is hard to compare. Ordinary yards gain little over the 350iB.
products.skipIf: You only blow leaves a few times a year.

products.name: Husqvarna 350BT Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 692 CFM gas backpack with brand-claimed lower emissions and better fuel use.
products.description:
The 350BT is the balanced gas backpack. It lists 692 CFM and, by the brand's claims, up to 60 percent lower emissions than a standard 2-stroke and 20 percent better fuel efficiency. A backpack puts the weight on your shoulders and hips, so a gas engine becomes tolerable for long sessions. It sits in the $200 to $500 tier.

It ranks fifth because those are Husqvarna's own figures, and it moves less air than the 580BTS and 150BT. Against the battery models, it needs no charging and gives you gas-length runtime.

Buy it for large lots where battery runtime would be a problem. The caveat: it needs fuel and maintenance, it is heavier than a battery handheld, and the emissions numbers are claims, not independent measurements.
products.idealFor: Large lots with long work sessions.

products.name: Husqvarna 580BTS Gas Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 1000 CFM, the highest airflow in the roundup, with a ventilated harness.
products.description:
The 580BTS is the airflow champion. It lists 1000 CFM, the top figure here, with a ventilated harness that spreads weight evenly and a tube-mounted throttle for easy control, in the $500 and up tier. A ventilated harness matters because a heavy backpack in summer heat is miserable.

It ranks sixth only because it is the most expensive and more machine than a normal yard needs. It beats every other pick on airflow, by a wide margin.

Buy it for commercial or very large properties, or deep autumn leaf cover. The caveat: a homeowner will not use all of it, and the price is the highest bracket. For a large residential lot, the 150BT does the job for far less.
products.skipIf: Your yard is a normal suburban lot.

products.name: Husqvarna 360BT Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A gas backpack with a ventilated harness with wide straps and an X-TORQUE engine.
products.description:
The 360BT is the comfort-first gas backpack. It features a ventilated, load-reducing harness with wide straps and an X-TORQUE engine meant to maximize power even at low RPM, in the $200 to $500 tier. Wide straps spread pressure, and a good harness is what separates a tolerable day from a miserable one.

It ranks below the 350BT because the listing gives no airflow figure. It sits pricier than the 150BT, which buys you the better harness.

A fit for long days wearing the machine. The caveat: look up the airflow before buying, because the listing leaves it out. If you want a clear spec to compare, the 350BT or 150BT give one.
products.idealFor: Long working days with the machine on your back.
products.skipIf: You want a clear airflow spec.

products.name: Husqvarna 150BT Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 765 CFM entry backpack with an ergonomic harness for long sessions.
products.description:
The 150BT is the entry gas backpack. It lists 765 CFM with an ergonomic harness for comfort over long sessions and a high-powered engine for demanding clearing, in the $200 to $500 tier. It costs less than the larger gas models and still beats the 350BT on airflow.

It ranks last because the battery models give similar airflow with less fuss. A 350iB moves 800 CFM with a trigger and no fuel.

A sensible gas option for a big yard on a budget. The caveat: it needs fuel and maintenance, and it is heavier than battery handhelds, so choose it only when battery runtime really would not cover your property.
pros: Cheaper than the larger gas models
products.idealFor: Big yards where gas runtime matters.

whatMatters.factor: Pick battery or gas by property size
whatMatters.detail: Battery tools start instantly and run quietly but stop when the pack runs out. Gas backpacks run as long as you carry fuel. For a typical suburban lot, battery is enough. For multiple acres, gas runtime and airflow matter more, and a second battery narrows the gap. Consider how far the leaves are from your tool storage.

whatMatters.factor: Look for CFM and MPH both
whatMatters.detail: CFM is volume of air and MPH is speed. Wet leaves need speed to lift, and big piles need volume to push. Check both on the listing, and be wary when only one appears. The 350iB lists 800 CFM and 200 MPH, which is a balanced pair for both piles and damp matted cover.

Two listings of the same blower can differ in whether a battery and charger ship. Read the box contents on the page and in the bullets, because a bare tool plus a separate battery and charger can cost far more than a kit. Compare the two 350iB listings carefully, since they share a name but not a box.

A handheld at 8.4 lbs still tires your arm over thirty minutes, while a backpack spreads weight across the shoulders. For long sessions, look for a ventilated harness with wide straps and a throttle within reach, and note that the 230iB is the lightest handheld here, while backpacks cost more but carry easier.

Figures like up to 60 percent lower emissions or 20 percent better fuel efficiency come from the manufacturer. Compare them across brands cautiously and sparingly, and use them as direction rather than guarantees. Independent measurements are rare in listings, so treat these as the brand's own statements and look for third-party reviews.

faq.q: Is a Husqvarna battery blower strong enough for a normal yard?
faq.a: Yes, for most. The Leaf Blaster 350iB lists 800 CFM and 200 MPH, which is plenty for most suburban lots, and the 230iB handles lighter work at 650 CFM. Check your leaf volume before choosing.

One includes a battery and charger in the kit, and the other is a lower-cost listing with less clear contents. Check what ships before buying, since the battery is the costly part and may be sold separately.

faq.q: Is the 230iB worth it over the 350iB?
faq.a: If you value weight, yes: it lists 8.4 lbs, the lightest here. The 350iB moves more air at 800 CFM versus 650, which helps with wet or deep leaves, at the cost of extra weight.

faq.q: Do I need a gas backpack blower?
faq.a: Only for very large properties, heavy leaf fall or all-day work. Battery handhelds like the 350iB cover most homes, and the 530iB serves heavier battery use. Gas backpacks pay off mainly on acreage.

faq.q: Are the emissions claims for the 350BT reliable?
faq.a: They are Husqvarna's own figures. Treat them as the brand's claims, not as independent measurements, when comparing the 350BT with other gas blowers, and do not rely on them alone.

faq.q: What does continuous boost on the 530iB mean?
faq.a: The listing says boost mode has no time limit, so it does not drop out after a short burst. That suits crews who keep the blower at full power for long stretches, but it will drain the battery faster.

finalTake: Buy the 350iB kit for most suburban yards, or the 230iB if weight matters more than airflow. The cheaper 350iB listing makes sense only if you already own Husqvarna batteries. Choose the 530iB for all-day battery work, and go to a gas backpack only for big acreage, with the 150BT as the value route and the 580BTS for maximum airflow.
